title: Playing blues and society versus colored dances
summary: The band was mostly a society band, played blues for colored dances in the same style, with different singing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Did a Pierron band ever play what you call blues, low down blues, or anything like that? Yeah.

Yeah, we played blues whenever the occasion presented. We played a color dance or something, you know. We played a blues. Did you play many color dances? Well, not many. We was mostly a society band around here. Most of our work was with the society people. See?
But you would use a different style when you played for a colored audience?

No, we played all the same style. It's just that, yeah. Maybe the singing you changed your style of singing like that, you know. But the blues was something that was for the, those days, the most of the common people. That you played blues for, you know. Outside of St. Louis blues, but I'm talking about the real stomp down blues. You know, like when you played the economy all over the collaborators or places like that where, you know.
How was T.O. on the blues? It was fine.
Who were the outstanding blues players in the band? Well, I don't know.
